A big NO for tourists.
We arrived at the emergency department last night with my boyfriend, who was suffering from severe food poisoning. He was vomiting repeatedly and was extremely weak. While waiting, he vomited several times into a trash bin in the waiting area, yet the staff showed no concern at all and no one checked on his condition.

When his name was finally called, I thought we were about to be seen. Instead, we were sent to another desk where around 10 more people were waiting. A nurse gave us a plastic chair and placed us in line with the others, despite the fact that my boyfriend continued vomiting and nearly fainted several times.

After about 50 minutes of waiting, I went to ask when he would be seen. The nurse replied rudely that there was only ONE doctor for everyone. At that point, we found the situation unacceptable and decided to leave. We went to another hospital, where he was treated immediately, received an IV drip, and was given the necessary medication.

This level of care was completely unacceptable, especially in an acute situation. I do not recommend this place.

This is an awful hospital. My boyfriend suffers from cluster headaches which is worse than migraines. They come on suddenly and severe and no medication helps. The only thing that is affective is oxygen. We told this to them and they said his oxygen is fine and to wait. We ask the wait time they said they don’t know. They didn’t show any empathy and were dismissive.

Took my fiancé here for a bad case of gastro/gastritis at 4am on the 24/8/2024. Very fast triaging and very helpful staff. The emergency room area was pretty clean and the staff listened to all our concerns. We were in and out within an hour after some IV medications and fluids. I’m a registered nurse from Australia and I was very pleased with the treatment we received from the doctor and nurses.
We cannot thank the staff enough for their care.

TERRIBLE! Ignorant staff. Came with my 8 years old who sprained ankle. Asked most irrelevant questions to register. Let us sit down saying a docotor will call call my son name. After 15min I asked how long we need to take xray so when doctor comes he can check. About 30 staff present and 3 patients. No one bother to tell us that doctor (apparently only one in the entire hospital)  is busy for more than onè hour. "Emergency"hospital where you wait for longer than one hour without being infomed about that. Pathetic!!!

Low standard on staff as well as on equipment. Charged me 1000 baht for cleaning one eye and didnt fix my problem though I told them it was the eye lid, not the eye Globe. 2 years ago it would have been 300 baht but since Prayut told them its ok to overcharge foreigners price went sky high.

Went from there to Bkk Hospital and such differens, they fliped the eye lid and took away the dirt and charged me 1500 baht.
50% more but huge differens in skill and equipment. Would have been 2500 baht but I told them I didnt want the medicine.
Bkk Hospital always tries to sell you a lot of medicine you dont actually need.
Incredibly quick and professional service for a very reasonable price. Treated severe dehydration and food poisoning through IV in under an hour.
Great service, although a bit slow but to be expected. Drs and intake spoke English, so that helped. Cost: 1200baht for Dr visit and prescription. Very reasonable.

Good afternoon! I've been trying to treat myself for three days, without success. I have high blood pressure, my left arm is failing, I have cervical osteochondrosis, and so on. I went to the hospital. I walked in at 10:50 and there wasn't a single empty chair. There were a lot of people, BUT by 11:50 I was already in the doctor's office. The appointment took five minutes (it's like a conveyor belt). I had my blood pressure checked beforehand (they have public access to the machines), and I got a prescription for the medications and services (they dispense the medications on-site). This took another 15 minutes because I needed an injection. I had to wait for my shot in the emergency room, but the whole thing took an average of two hours. Bottom line: the lobby was almost empty. Arrive at the clinic after 12:00 if possible. Service was fast, everything was clear, the staff was friendly, and they prescribed medication based on my symptoms, making me want to live the next day. And it only cost 1,050 baht for a bunch of pills, ointment (not pictured), the appointment, and an intravenous injection. Thank you so much for your help!

Highly not recommended.

I got water in my ear, and after waiting a long time outside the clinic, the doctor finally arrived with a cup of coffee. He glanced at my ear and said they couldn't handle it, telling me to go to a private hospital, which ended up costing me 600 baht.

I went to another hospital a couple of days ago, and they prescribed oral medication and ear drops, costing less than 300 baht in total.

Two stars for the service staff: a young woman helped with English translation throughout, and the pharmacy nurse was very helpful in asking about my allergies and filling out my medical card.

They quickly cleaned and stitched up a laceration from hitting a rock in the water. The instruments were sterile and sealed, and they opened them in front of me. During the procedure, they checked for allergies, chronic illnesses, and my general condition. They gave me the necessary medications and instructions for use. Cash only; they don't work with insurance companies. They even gave me a tetanus shot.

I've been here. Basically, one person can't figure everything out. Same here. Mostly locals come, tourists make up about 10%. People come for prescriptions and for injuries. Some fell off a bike, some got injured in the pool. That's what they know. But they couldn't clean my ear. They just don't know how.

My child had a cough, so we just went in to make sure his lungs were clear. The wait, doctor's appointment, payment, and medication collection took 1:20.
Overall, it was very quick. The appointment and cough medicine cost 609 baht.

It might seem a little strange to Europeans, but everything was actually fine. They understand and speak English and are willing to help. I paid €40 for wound cleaning, stitching, bandaging, and a tetanus shot.
The nurses work quickly and speak politely, which makes the patients feel comfortable and impressed.
